title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the surrounding pages. ξ ∈ Π̂_{0,3}, the free profinite group on ℓ0, ℓ1. It is mapped into SL(2,Ẑ)', apparently the principal congruence subgroup of level 2, with ℓ0 ↦ (1 2; 0 1) and ℓ1 ↦ (1 0; 2 1). ξ is attached to a solution of the 'équation des lacets', an automorphism of Π̂_{0,3} with multiplier p = 2σ+1 ∈ Ẑ*. On the previous page the image matrix (A B; C D) of ξ must have D ∈ Ẑ*. D is expressed through the matrix λ' = (a b; c d) of λ, an element of SL(2,ℤ) defined up to sign, which determines p.

Point 1 (end). p is the inverse of D up to sign: D = δ(c²+cd+d²). The sign δ ∈ {±1} is fixed by D ≡ δ (mod 3). This is consistent: for c even, d odd, c²+cd+d² ≡ (c−d)² (mod 3), so it is ≡ 1 mod 3 whenever it is a unit.

Point 3, consistency check against arithmetic. Π_ℚ = Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) acts on Π̂_{0,3}, and the cyclotomic character χ: Π_ℚ → Ẑ* is surjective. So every p ∈ Ẑ* must occur, i.e. be of the form 1/D (equivalently D):
- D = c²+cd+d² if p ≡ 1 (mod 3);
- D = −(3(c²+cd)+d²) if p ≡ −1 (mod 3);
- with c, d ∈ Ẑ, c ≡ 0 and d ≡ 1 (mod 2).
By Ẑ = ∏ ℤ_ℓ this reduces to a local check, stated as a Corollary:
- ℓ ≠ 3: every unit of ℤ_ℓ is represented by both forms.
  - ℓ ≥ 5: a unimodular binary form represents all units.
  - ℓ = 2: x²+xy+y² is the norm form of the unramified extension ℤ_2[ω], whose norms of units 1+2O already exhaust ℤ_2*; this allows c even, d odd.
- ℓ = 3: the form represents exactly the units ≡ 1 (mod 3). This is the norm group of the ramified extension ℤ_3[ω], equal to 1+3ℤ_3, of index 2. Hence c²+cd+d² ↔ p ≡ 1 and −(3c²+3cd+d²) ↔ p ≡ −1, mutually exclusive.

Margin 'on s'en fiche du −3(c²+cd)+d² !'. Indeed 3c²+3cd+d² = x²+xy+y² with x = c, y = c+d, so it is the same form. The parity conditions are also preserved (c even, c+d odd). The second form is therefore redundant; only the overall sign δ matters.

Point 4, opening the next page. At the level of SL(2,Ẑ)' the 'equation in λ' is 'anodyne': it only says c²+cd+d² ∈ Ẑ*. One might hope to lift such congruence-level solutions to Π̂_{0,3} and build large families of solutions. The next page admits failure: no explicit solution was found besides u = 1 and u = τ_∞ (identity and complex conjugation). It then asks whether a solution at the SL(2,Ẑ)' level always lifts to Π̂_{0,3} with the same σ.
errors: No mathematical error. The two quadratic forms are equivalent (3c²+3cd+d² = c²+c(c+d)+(c+d)²), so the case split by form is redundant; the margin note acknowledges this.

Transcription sign slips: the image writes D = −3(c²+cd) ∓ d², and the first occurrence should read −3(c²+cd)−d² (as the Corollary has it). The margin's '−3(c²+cd)+d²' is likewise a slip for −(3(c²+cd)+d²).

ideas.what: Image in the level-2 congruence quotient SL(2,Ẑ)' of the Galois/GT-type action on Π̂_{0,3}: the multiplier (cyclotomic character) is read off as 1/D, with D a value of the norm form c²+cd+d² up to sign
ideas.modern_name: Image of Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) or GT in the congruence (metabelian-type) quotient; cyclotomic character recovered from a congruence image
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Drinfeld; later work on GT and its congruence/metabelian quotients (Ihara, Nakamura, Schneps and others)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (partially circulated); Esquisse d'un programme only qualitatively

ideas.what: Every unit of Ẑ is ± a value of x²+xy+y² with x even, y odd; ℓ=3 forces the sign by p mod 3
ideas.modern_name: Local representation of units by the norm form of ℤ[ω] (unramified at 2, ramified at 3)

ideas.what: Hope of lifting congruence-level solutions to explicit solutions in Π̂_{0,3}; failure to construct any beyond identity and complex conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Lack of explicit elements of GT^ / Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) acting on F̂2; lifting from congruence quotients
ideas.usually_credited_to: Recognized open problem in GT theory (Drinfeld 1990, Ihara, Schneps, Lochak)

missed.claim: Grothendieck poses (continued on the next page) a lifting question. Given a solution of the equation at the level of SL(2,Ẑ)', is there a lift to Π̂_{0,3} satisfying the full 'équation des lacets' with the same σ? The congruence-level constraint is only that c²+cd+d² is a unit.
missed.quote: on pourrait espérer tenir une méthode pour construire ... des gros paquets de solutions
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It amounts to asking how far the congruence quotient detects GT^. Related lifting questions are studied for GT and its quotients, but this exact formulation, via the norm form of ℤ[ω], seems to be only implicit in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine local computation of units represented by the Eisenstein norm form, used as a consistency check of the cyclotomic character in a GT-like setting. The confession of failure to construct explicit solutions mirrors a well-known open difficulty. Nothing appears substantially new.
transcription_corrections: The first formula for the second form reads −3(c²+cd)−d² (written D = −3(c²+cd) ∓ d²), not −3(c²+cd)+d².
The opening line includes a struck-out fragment 'mieux les a…' and a deleted '(voir D=3(c²+cd)+d²)'. The inserted phrase reads 'où δ ∈ {±1} est déterminé par la condition D ≡ δ (3)'.
In the Corollary, 'c,d ∈ Ẑ_ℓ' should read ℤ_ℓ; the hat appears to be a slip.
The margin note reads 'on s'en fiche du −3(c²+cd)+d² !' — note the self-recognition that the second form is redundant.
'ces qui sont mutuellement exclusifs' should read 'cas qui sont mutuellement exclusifs'.
